pr_title: Add Camellia CBC CTS mode support to EVP layer
pr_body:
Fixes #16276

The provider related AES CTS code has been renamed so that it can be
shared with Camellia. The only real difference is the underlying cbc
cipher that is used (which is pointed to in a generic manner via the hw
pointer).

pr_comments:
The encryption test vectors listed here in
https://mirror.unpad.ac.id/ietf/internet-drafts/draft-ietf-krb-wg-camellia-cts-00.txt
are missing a vital piece of information.. which is listed here.
https://www.rfc-editor.org/errata_search.php?rfc=6803
Tests and Documentation added. Commits have been split up.

It took longer to derive the test vectors than it did to write the actual code..
The derived key for camellia CTS seems to use KBKDF whereas another RFC's for KRB uses KRB5KDF (sigh!)
Even if this doesnt go in for 3.0 there are some bug fixes in this PR that probably should be included..

> Even if this doesnt go in for 3.0 there are some bug fixes in this PR that probably should be included..

Could you please split those out into a separate PR? I do not think this can go into 3.0 as a whole.
I'd like to have it in 3.0 (otherwise we possibly will have to apply it as a downstream patch), but I agree that the bugfixes are worth separating if possible.

> > Even if this doesnt go in for 3.0 there are some bug fixes in this PR that probably should be included..
> 
> Could you please split those out into a separate PR? I do not think this can go into 3.0 as a whole.

The PR really has 3 parts:
1) Move existing CTS code into a separate file so that it can be shared. Make AES_CTS use this.
2) A direct copy of the AES code to setup CAMELLIA - the only change really is the names passed to the tables
3) Bug fixes 
  (i) Handle a 16 byte input  for CS3 as normal CBC instead of erroring.
  (ii) the decrypt was not returning the correct updated iv.

We should be doing (1) and (3) at least I think..
(2) Can be done later - but I don't see it causing any issue as it is all shared code..

> It took longer to derive the test vectors than it did to write the actual code..
> The derived key for camellia CTS seems to use KBKDF whereas another RFC's for KRB uses KRB5KDF (sigh!)

The key-derivation process is rather intrinsic to the RFC 3961 cryptographic suite ... which you should not be expected to know just from the request being made of openssl.  Which KDF to use is a property of the encryption or checksum type, and as we define new encryption/checksum algorithms we try to take advantage of improvements in KDF design as well.

24 hours has passed since 'approval: done' was set, but as this PR has been updated in that time the label 'approval: ready to merge' is not being automatically set.  Please review the updates and set the label manually.
Do we have any decision on this?

Discussed on the call.
Waiting on OTC vote result (and for the OTC vote text to be emailed out @mattcaswell ).

Thanks for making this PR.  It (and the AES CTS code that exists already) appears to work with krb5 in my [test branch](https://github.com/frozencemetery/krb5/commit/8f79e68fbeaf88fbcd7857e060c9b48f472c3209).
With @beldmit's vote cast the decision is clear and you can close the vote and proceed imho.

issue_context.title: Add Camellia CTS implementation to default provider
issue_context.body:
We are missing Camellia CTS in the high level API which was possible to do with the old APIs.
See also #16235
comments: I am having a look. It doesn't look too hard to refactor this to handle both cases..

@frozencemetery I am looking at test vectors in
https://mirror.unpad.ac.id/ietf/internet-drafts/draft-ietf-krb-wg-camellia-cts-00.txt

And dont seem to be getting the right results for  Sample encryptions (all using the default cipher state):
````
   Plaintext: 1
   Random confounder:
       6F 2F C3 C2 A1 66 FD 88 98 96 7A 83 DE 95 96 D9
   128-bit Camellia key:
       50 27 BC 23 1D 0F 3A 9D 23 33 3F 1C A6 FD BE 7C
   Ciphertext:
       84 2D 21 FD 95 03 11 C0 DD 46 4A 3F 4B E8 D6 DA
       88 A5 6D 55 9C 9B 47 D3 F9 A8 50 67 AF 66 15 59
       B8
`````
I was assuming this translates to:

````
IV =  00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
PT =  6F2FC3C2A166FD8898967A83DE9596D931 (cofounder || pt)
KEY = 5027BC231D0F3A9D23333F1CA6FDBE7C (Is this right??)
CT =  842D21FD950311C0DD464A3F4BE8D6DA88 (first bytes of above CIphertext)
````

Any ideas where I am going wrong here?
It appears that the key is the base key - the missing data is the usage,,,

>  https://mirror.unpad.ac.id/ietf/internet-drafts/draft-ietf-krb-wg-camellia-cts-00.txt

For what it's worth, that's an early draft of [RFC 6803](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6803).

As I read section 6, that vector becomes:

    IV = <all zeroes>
    PT = 6F 2F C3 C2 A1 66 FD 88 98 96 7A 83 DE 95 96 D9 01
    KEY (Ke): 50 27 BC 23 1D 0F 3A 9D 23 33 3F 1C A6 FD BE 7C
    CT = 84 2D 21 FD 95 03 11 C0 DD 46 4A 3F 4B E8 D6 DA 88

assuming by CT you mean what the draft calls C.

The only difference I spot is that the last octet of PT needs to be a full octet: you have 1, I have 01.

If that doesn't help, we can ask the document author.
Right after hitting submit, another thought: the "key" may not be "Ke" but rather base-key.  So you'd need to derive Ke (and Ki, if you were doing the MAC part) from it using the KDF.

Yeah it was the base key.. Test vectors are now in the PR.
The missing usage was what threw me initially.

review_comments: This effectively limits this generic CTS implementation to block ciphers with 128 bit block size. Maybe add a comment above.
